headline: DJI Osmo Pocket 4P promises 17 stops of dynamic range, rivaling cinema cams
summary: DJI's new pro gimbal camera aims to deliver cinema-grade dynamic range with its 17-stop claim. It features dual cameras, including a 3x zoom lens, and introduces a new D-Log2 mode.
details: DJI has revealed more details for its Osmo Pocket 4P pro gimbal camera, promising an impressive 17 stops of dynamic range. This figure, if verified, would place it on par with high-end cinema cameras from brands like Arri and surpass other consumer-level cameras. A new D-Log2 mode is also introduced to fully utilize this extended dynamic range.

The Osmo Pocket 4P features two cameras: a regular wide lens similar to the mainstream Osmo Pocket 4, and a 3x zoom lens. The 3x zoom lens has a 60mm full-frame equivalent focal length, making it suitable for portraits and product photography, complementing the main camera's estimated 20mm equivalent.
In addition to the classic black, the Osmo Pocket 4P will also be available in white. This new color option matches its rival, the Insta360 Luna Ultra, offering more choice for buyers.

While some key specifications like price, resolution, and frame rates remain officially unannounced for global markets, the camera is reportedly already on sale in China. A release date for Europe or North America is expected early next quarter.
